questions.question: P is thrice as efficient as Q and hence completes the work in 20 days less than the number of days taken by Q. In how many days the work will be completed by both of them together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of P to Q is 3 : 1, so their time ratio is 1 : 3.

Difference in time ratio parts = 3 − 1 = 2 parts.

Given difference is 20 days, so 2 parts = 20 days ⇒ 1 part = 10 days.

Time taken by P = 10 days, Time taken by Q = 30 days.

Time for both together = (10 × 30) ÷ (10 + 30) = 300 ÷ 40 = 7.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P is thrice as efficient as Q.

Difference in days taken by Q and P = 20 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

Since Work is constant, Time is inversely proportional to Efficiency.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let time taken by P be x days.

⇒ Then, time taken by Q = 3x days.

⇒ Difference in time = 3x − x = 20 days.

⇒ 2x = 20 ⇒ x = 10 days.

⇒ P takes 10 days, Q takes 30 days.

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 50°, BE and CF are perpendiculars on AC and AB at E and F, respectively. BE and CF intersect at H. The bisectors of ∠HBC and ∠HCB intersect at P. ∠BPC is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle at Orthocenter (H): ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A

Angle at Incenter (P) of ΔHBC: ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

Combining the two: ∠BPC = 90° + (180° − ∠A) / 2 = 180° − ∠A / 2

Substituting ∠A = 50°: ∠BPC = 180° − 50° / 2 = 180° − 25° = 155°.

**∴ The correct answer is 155°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠A = 50° in ΔABC. BE and CF are altitudes intersecting at H. P is the intersection of bisectors of ∠HBC and ∠HCB.

**Formula Used:**

1. Angle formed by altitudes at orthocenter: ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A

2. Angle formed by interior angle bisectors in ΔHBC: ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9586d56be3ec3232d064967b43f1d22e705be8661895ac6a6edd8d922b6ec714.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In quadrilateral AFHE, ∠AFH = 90° and ∠AEH = 90°.

⇒ Sum of angles in AFHE = 360°

⇒ ∠A + ∠AFH + ∠AEH + ∠FHE = 360°

⇒ 50° + 90° + 90° + ∠FHE = 360°

⇒ ∠FHE = 360° − 230° = 130°

⇒ ∠BHC = ∠FHE = 130° (Vertically opposite angles)

⇒ In ΔHBC, P is the incenter because it is the intersection of angle bisectors.

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + 130° / 2

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + 65° = 155°.

**∴ The correct answer is 155°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Orthocenter Property

The angle subtended by any side at the orthocenter (H) is supplementary to the opposite vertex angle: ∠BHC + ∠A = 180°.

Incenter Angle Formula

The angle formed by interior angle bisectors at the incenter (I) is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A / 2.

Circumcenter Angle Formula

The angle subtended by a side at the circumcenter (O) is twice the angle at the vertex: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Ex-center Angle Formula

The angle formed by the intersection of exterior angle bisectors at the ex-center (E) is ∠BEC = 90° − ∠A / 2.</p

questions.question: Simplify (6.1 times 6.1 times 6.1-1)/(6.1 times 6.1+6.1+1)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression follows the algebraic pattern: (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²) = a − b.

Here, replacing a with 6.1 and b with 1 perfectly matches the terms in the question.

Directly calculating a − b gives the final result.

Result = 6.1 − 1 = 5.1

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (6.1 × 6.1 × 6.1 − 1) ÷ (6.1 × 6.1 + 6.1 + 1)

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Numerator = (6.1)³ − 1³

⇒ Denominator = (6.1)² + 6.1 × 1 + 1²

⇒ Expression = [(6.1)³ − 1³] ÷ [(6.1)² + 6.1 + 1]

⇒ Applying the formula for the difference of cubes in the numerator:

⇒ Expression = [(6.1 − 1)((6.1)² + 6.1 × 1 + 1²)] ÷ [(6.1)² + 6.1 + 1]

⇒ The term ((6.1)² + 6.1 + 1) is common in both numerator and denominator.

⇒ Canceling the common term, we are left with:

⇒ Expression = 6.1 − 1

⇒ Expression = 5.1

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Formula

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). This identity is frequently used to rapidly simplify fraction expressions containing positive cubic terms.

Difference of Squares Formula

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). It helps in instantly factoring and reducing fractions containing squared differences.

Perfect Square Formulas

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². These are primary tools for algebraic expansion and solving polynomial equations.

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the circle. If ∠DBC = 29°, then ∠BAD = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD where BC is the diameter, the angle at the vertex A is related to ∠DBC by the direct formula:

∠BAD = 90° + ∠DBC

Given ∠DBC = 29°

⇒ ∠BAD = 90° + 29° = 119°

**∴ The correct answer is 119°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

BC is the diameter of the circle.

∠DBC = 29°.

**Formula Used:**

1. Angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is 90° (Angle in a semicircle).

2. The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d218f10e84edbbd223a89fbb05525673b28e5ecc9b1b83d7bd36004277489649.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since BC is the diameter, the angle subtended by it at point D is 90°.

⇒ ∴ ∠BDC = 90°

⇒ In ΔBCD, the sum of all internal angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠DBC + ∠BDC + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ 29° + 90° + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ 119° + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 119° = 61°

⇒ In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, opposite angles ∠BAD and ∠BCD sum to 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD + 61° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − 61° = 119°

**∴ The correct answer is 119°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

Any angle subtended by the diameter at the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

For any quadrilateral whose vertices lie on a circle, the sum of opposite internal angles is exactly 180°.

Exterior Angle of a Cyclic Quadrilateral

An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is 180°.</p

What are Causes?

Causes are the conditions under which an event occurs.

For example, can you guess the causes for the following? 

The police increasing security around the President's house.

Lots of people buying a particularly expensive brand of washing machines around Diwali. Easily, we can guess the causes for the above events. 

There were reports of threats against the President. 

There was a high discount or sale for that brand during Diwali.

Sufficient & Necessary Conditions:

In a cause and effect question, the cause is the sufficient condition. It is assumed that the sufficient condition of the occurrence of the events must include the different necessary conditions as well. 

A necessary condition is one that must be satisfied for the occurrence of an event. 

E.g. You must adhere to the deadline to get your work appraised. 

This means if you get your work appraised, you have to adhere to the deadline. Or; if you do not adhere to the deadline, you do not get your work appraised. 

A condition is called a sufficient condition if in a certain event, you are satisfied with the results.

E.g. Being human is a sufficient condition for being a mammal. The act of being a human is not possible unless one is also a mammal. But it is not necessary that being human is a necessary condition for being a mammal.

questions.question: Comparatively higher value of BOD indicates
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• BOD stands for** Biochemical Oxygen Demand**.
 
• It is the** amount of dissolved oxygen** **required by aerobic biological organisms** to **break down organic material** present in a given water sample at a certain temperature over a specific time period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Water with a lot of **organic matter contains more microbes** that decompose the organic matter.
 
• Such a water body with **high organic matter will have high BOD.**
 
• BOD is high because **more dissolved O₂ is required by ​aerobic microbes to break down organic material.**
 
• Water with **high BOD will have less oxygen** dissolved in it **because most is being used by microorganisms.**
 
• If the microorganism needs more oxygen for decomposing the organic material, then **less of it is available for aquatic organisms.**
 
• This **decreases the number of aquatic animals** in the water because less oxygen is left for them.
 
• More **BOD indicates more pollution.**
 
• Water bodies with **high BOD have more microbes and organic matter.**
 
• **High BOD harms aquatic life.**

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Sewage water from our homes contains a lot of organic matter** in the form of fecal matter, kitchen waste, cloth and paper fibers, *etc*.
 
• These are **first treated by microbes in sewage treatment plants** before releasing in water bodies to reduce the BOD.
 
• **If they are not treated and directly released** into the water body, the **microbes and organic matter in the water body increases.**
 
• This **leads to a higher value of BOD** because the microbes use O₂ to decompose organic matter.
 
• **Fresh water and tap water are very clean** and do not have much organic matter.
 
• **Fresh water sources are sea, river, and rainwater**. 
 
• They are usually formed from melting glaciers and rainwater and hence are very clean.
 
• Tap water in our homes is usually treated or is underground water, both of which are clean source and do not have much organic matter.
 
• **Marine water is from oceans** and is very salty.
 
• They are very large water bodies, so, their BOD does not change with small deposition of organic matter.

Hence, the water body with high BOD indicated that it is sewage water.__
